title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
summary: In real-world applications like egocentric recording, visual accessibility, and surveillance review, visual evidence for Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) is often only partially captured. A reliable model should match its response to the evidence: answering when sufficient, guessing from visible clues when partial, and abstaining when absent. Yet existing benchmarks enforce a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial evidence unmeasured and obscuring whether failures arise from missing evidence or misjudging sufficiency. We introduce ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark to (1) separate perceiving evidence from judging sufficiency, and (2) validate our diagnosis via targeted fine-tuning. ClueProbe comprises 1,721 human-annotated questions across 598 natural videos, labeled Answerable, Guessable, or Unanswerable, alongside controlled perturbations altering wording or visual input. Evaluating 10 open-source and proprietary Video LLMs reveals that failures stem from judgment rather than perception: models perceive the evidence yet lack graded sufficiency awareness, answering or refusing outright while rarely guessing from partial clues. Targeted fine-tuning shows that this reflects missing supervision rather than insufficient capacity: supervising the guess level lifts appropriate guessing from 1.6% to 40.4% without extra false refusals, whereas conventional refusal tuning rejects 92% of guessable questions. Data and code will be released at https://github.com/suat-llm/ClueProbe.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ClueProbe 诊断基准，将视频问答的证据状态分为可回答、可猜测与不可回答，并用针对性微调检验 Video LLM 是否缺乏分级充分性判断。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关联证据充分性评估与作答/停止决策，区分「看见证据」和「判断够不够」，可供核查 LVR 中 STOP 机制、视觉证据筛选及分级监督对输出时机的影响。

title: Lost in the Grid: Where Multimodal LLMs Fail Between Seeing and Planning
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel at static visual understanding and are increasingly applied to spatial planning, where a model interprets a visual layout and outputs an action sequence to reach a goal. Grid games are a common testbed for this ability because their rules are explicit and a solver can verify every move. Yet existing benchmarks mostly report end-to-end success rates, which hide whether a failure stems from visual perception, rule application, or multi-step planning. We introduce GridProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that 1) locates the failing stage between visual perception and planning and 2) verifies the diagnosis by targeted fine-tuning. On Sokoban, GridProbe pairs end-to-end solving with four probes (recognition, localization, single-step prediction, and state tracking) and gives every board both as an image and as an equivalent text grid. Evaluating seven MLLMs on Sokoban and a maze game reveals distinct bottlenecks behind similar success rates: proprietary models are limited by multi-step planning, whereas open-source models are limited by rule application or by visual grid indexing, i.e., counting rows and columns. Planning failures also hide perception failures: when planning is easier, the visual cost of the same model grows from 7.6 to 37.7 points. The diagnosis identifies what to train: fine-tuning only the vision module of the perception-limited model on board reading raises its interactive Sokoban success 3.5-fold (5.8% to 20.4%) and transfers zero-shot to the unseen maze game (single-turn success 13.8% to 67.1%), whereas the same data does not help a rule-limited model and training on solver solutions brings no gain. We will release the benchmark and code at https://github.com/suat-llm/GridProbe.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 GridProbe 诊断基准，在 Sokoban 与迷宫任务上把「视觉感知—规划」链路拆成识别、定位、单步预测与状态跟踪四类探针，并同时提供图像与等价文本网格；再用定向微调验证诊断结论，发现闭源模型瓶颈在多步规划、开源模型反而卡在规则应用或行列索引，且视觉代价在规划变易时从 7.6 升至 37.7 分。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉细节保留与「看/想」贡献分配：其探针与图文等价设计可供核查视觉证据筛选与失败归因，微调视觉模块带来的 3.5 倍提升与零样本迁移也为「该训练哪一部分」提供对照参照。

title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
summary: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.

AI.brief_summary: 究问「多模态模型能否用图像思考」：让模型先描述所需辅助图，再由生成器出图，并与原图一起作答；在 13 组视觉语言模型与生成器配对中平均准确率下降 3.7 个百分点，十个任务中九个退步。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接以负结果检验「生成视觉证据辅助推理」这一假设，与视觉证据筛选、生成视觉旁路是否被答案真正使用密切相关；ERQA 经十次编辑后反升 3 点等任务差异，可供核查生成内容何时进入推理状态。

title: Attributing Agentic Failure in Reasoning Vision-Language Models with Interactive 2D Environments
summary: Agentic benchmarks report a success rate that confounds distinct causes of failure: misreading the environment, never working out how components of the environment operates, operating the components in the wrong order, and failing to recover from a mistake, each of which calls for a different fix. We present an early preview of MultiNet v2.0-Gridworld - an interactive maze environment built for attribution rather than ranking. Four different types of mechanisms, namely key-door pairs, switch-gate pairs, distractors and decoys, and ordered combinations of these mechanisms, can be added, modified, or removed independently while the renderer, the action space, and the scoring function stay fixed. A breadth-first search over the joint state of position, facing direction, inventory, and mechanism state gives every instance an exact optimal action count, which sets its difficulty and grades unfinished episodes. We fix the evaluation protocol on 15 held-out mazes over 540 episodes, then evaluate three vision-language models on 50 mazes. They solve 6 of 150 episodes, 45 of the 50 mazes were not solved by any model, and no episode containing a switch-gate mechanism was solved.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建交互式 2D 迷宫环境 MultiNet v2.0-Gridworld，通过独立增删钥匙-门、开关-闸门等机制组件，并用 BFS 给出精确最优步数来确定难度和评分，以便把 VLM 智能体失败归因到读环境、理解组件、操作顺序、错误恢复等不同原因，而非只报成功率；三个 VLM 在 50 个迷宫、150 个 episode 中仅解出 6 个。
AI.relevance_reason: 可独立调节的视觉机制组合与失败类型归因，可供核查 VLM 的视觉证据使用、状态与操作顺序推理及停止决策，与 LVR 关注的视觉信息坍缩和贡献分配线索相通；但未涉及 latent 状态生成，主要价值在诊断评测设计。

title: Measuring and Predicting Image-Token Repair Boundaries in Vision-Language Models
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, 17 tables; supplementary material included
summary: Degraded images make vision-language models answer wrongly. Using synthetic paired blur, noise, and low light, we trace which clean image states can still repair those answers from the vision encoder through the language model. In four encoder models, 12 to 23 ranked tokens recover half of the full-patch effect, whereas random orders require four to fifteen times as many; encoder-free Gemma needs 22.2 versus 53.1. Full-block repair expires at a model-specific language-model crossing. The matched reverse-direction intervention is algebraically identical to text-token restoration, so its gap from image restoration measures a redundancy band rather than an independent predictor. A clean-image gray-ablation crossing independently predicts held-out repair with 1.53-layer error, against 3.65 for shared depth. Gemma MMBench has the only large attention-to-repair point gap; Gemma GQA does not. Restormer provides a non-oracle consistency check on two models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究退化图像下哪些干净图像 token 或其内部状态能修复 VLM 的错误答案，追踪从视觉编码器到语言模型的修复边界，并检验层深度、注意力与冗余能否预测修复效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接考察视觉 token 对答案的因果修复作用、逐层作用边界及注意力结构，与视觉证据筛选、latent 内容使用和深度／位置效应高度相关，可供核查其修复度量及冗余带结论。

title: ViCARD: Visual Credit Assignment with Reward-Gated Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
summary: Visual reasoning requires models to identify relevant visual evidence and use it to derive correct answers. Outcomebased reinforcement learning (RL) faces two key challenges in this regime: it yields no learning signal when perceptual errors cause all sampled responses to fail, and it broadcasts a uniform advantage across every token within a response. Conversely, while visual self-distillation offers dense guidance from evidence-centered image crops, student learning from token distributions alone often fails to elicit correct final answers. Motivated by an audit of training rollouts that exposes these complementary failure modes, we introduce ViCARD (Visual Credit Assignment with RewardGated Distillation), which integrates per-token visual supervision with verified correctness rewards. For each rollout group, we leverage a teacher with its input image cropped to the relevant visual area, and use this to provide per-token supervision to the student while also valuing correctness. If all sampled rollouts fail, ViCARD samples an additional crop-teacher answer and activates on-policy distillation only if that answer is correct. Together, these mechanisms provide fine-grained visual credit within informative reward groups and a learning signal for otherwise uninformative all-fail groups. Extensive comparisons across model scales demonstrate that ViCARD improves fine-grained visual reasoning performance over RL and distillation baselines, while retaining broad visual reasoning capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 ViCARD，将基于证据裁剪图像的教师逐 token 视觉监督与可验证正确性奖励结合，并在采样全失败时以裁剪教师的正确答案为门控条件启用 on-policy 蒸馏，用于多模态推理训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐 token 视觉信用分配与「答案是否真正使用视觉证据」的贡献分配问题直接相关，全失败组的奖励门控蒸馏也触及稀疏监督下的证据筛选；但监督落在输出分布而非 latent 推理状态，与 LVR 状态生成的联系待核查。

title: HumblePRM: Improving VLM Abstention in Ambiguous Situations through Process Reward Modeling
summary: Reliable deployment of Vision Language Models (VLMs) requires that a model's expressed confidence remain grounded in what it can actually see, and that it recognize when the visual evidence is too ambiguous to commit to a confident response. Standard post-training uses outcome reward models (ORMs) that supervise only the final decision, rewarding a confident answer regardless of whether the image supports one, while existing methods either tend to detect uncertainty post-hoc or assume an objective verdict always exists. We instead split multimodal reasoning into two stages: perception, where the model must factually describe the scene, and calibration, where it must judge whether that evidence is sufficient to commit to a conclusion. We introduce HumblePRM, a lightweight process reward model (PRM) that scores each stage independently, rewarding agreement between evidence and expressed confidence rather than outcome correctness alone. Training with HumblePRM increases abstention due to uncertainty on ambiguous inputs considerably while leaving accuracy on clear images roughly unchanged. We also find that the improvement transfers to Gemma 4 E4B, a larger, popular edge model. Our findings show that process reward supervision is a promising route to VLMs with better calibrated abstention, ensuring more reliability rather than unpredictable behavior.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将多模态推理拆为感知描述与校准两个阶段，提出轻量过程奖励模型 HumblePRM，分别打分并要求视觉证据与表达置信度一致，以提升 VLM 在证据模糊时的弃答率。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接涉及「视觉证据是否充分、何时停止或弃答」的决策，其分阶段过程监督可供核查如何把证据筛选与置信校准接入 latent 推理状态。

title: Streaming Tax: Can Streaming VLMs Replace Their Offline Parents?
summary: Most vision-language models (VLMs) specialize in offline video understanding; in contrast, their post-trained versions, streaming VLMs, can perform live interactions. We investigate whether streaming VLMs can replace their offline parent models on offline tasks. Such replacement could reduce deployment costs and improve efficiency. We propose Streaming Tax to systematically evaluate streaming VLMs on offline tasks. Our exploration spans three core dimensions: understanding, trustworthiness, and generalization across 15 benchmarks. Our findings reveal a critical gap between offline capability preservation and practical replaceability. This gap emerges at two stages: streaming adaptation can alter trustworthy behavior even when offline understanding is largely preserved, while the native streaming protocol can introduce further performance losses. Our analyses show that some of these losses arise from restricted access to historical visual evidence and failures to deliver usable responses. Importantly, regarding safety, streaming models often leave both harmful and legitimate requests unanswered rather than genuinely refusing unsafe ones. We then propose Stream++, a training-free plugin to improve streaming VLMs on offline tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Streaming Tax，在 15 个基准上从理解、可信度与泛化三个维度，系统检验 streaming VLM 能否在离线任务上替代其 offline 父模型，并分析性能损失来源，最后给出免训练插件 Stream++。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「历史视觉证据访问受限」与安全请求未被真正拒绝的失败分析，可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节能否保留在内部状态、证据获取成本与停止决策等问题；但未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成，联系偏诊断层面。

title: EvOrderBench: When do sampled frames establish event order?
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are often asked which of two actions in a video happened first, given only a few sampled frames. Such frames can show that both actions occurred without showing which came first, so a reliable model should state an order only when the frames establish it. Forced-choice temporal benchmarks treat every input as answerable and reward lucky guesses, while answerability benchmarks do not separate frames that miss an action from frames that show both actions but not their order. We introduce EvOrderBench, a real-video benchmark of 579 event families. Each family fixes an episode and a question and varies only the frames: of two four-frame inputs, only one establishes the order, and two six-frame inputs extend the other one with either the frames that resolve the order or frames that do not. Every input is labeled for whether its frames establish each action and their order. Across sixteen open-weight configurations and three closed-source references, the best open models order nearly as accurately as the references when the frames establish the order, but withhold correctly on at most 83% of the inputs where they do not, against at least 90% for every reference; forced-choice accuracy cannot reveal this gap. Open models withhold mainly when the frames show neither action; once the frames show one or both, most of them commit to an order. Thinking narrows the gap, even when it is switched on within a single checkpoint, mainly by separating sufficient from insufficient evidence rather than by making models more cautious overall. Accurate ordering thus does not imply knowing when the frames fall short, and benchmarks should reward withholding alongside ordering.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 EvOrderBench：以 579 个真实视频事件族控制采样帧，标注帧是否足以确定动作发生及其先后顺序，并比较 16 个开源与 3 个闭源 VLM 的排序和拒答表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准直接检验 VLM 能否在视觉证据不足时停止作答，与 LVR 的证据充分性判断、STOP 决策及内部状态是否保留顺序信息密切相关；其“会排序不等于会拒答”的诊断可供核查。

title: Read Before You Use: Improving Visual Memory Utilization in Vision-Language Models
summary: Multimodal memory enables long-horizon vision-language agents to preserve and retrieve past experiences. While prior research has focused on memory construction and retrieval, effectively using the provided memory remains a challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We find that VLMs often fail to answer downstream questions even when sufficient multimodal evidence is provided. To investigate why VLMs struggle, we replace memory images with reference captions and observe substantial performance gains, suggesting difficulties in reading visual evidence directly. However, model-generated captions may omit critical information, limiting this approach in practice. These limitations motivate a closer examination of memory utilization, revealing failures in both evidence reading and downstream question answering. Building on this distinction, we propose \textbf{MemRU}, a two-stage training framework that improves evidence reading through supervised fine-tuning (Read SFT) and downstream evidence utilization through Group Relative Policy Optimization (Use GRPO). Experimental results demonstrate that our 8B model generalizes across three unseen multimodal memory systems, outperforming Qwen3-VL-32B and approaching GPT-5-mini.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断视觉语言模型在多模态记忆场景中「有证据却答不对」的问题，区分证据读取与下游作答两类失败，发现用文字描述替换记忆图像可显著提升表现，并提出两阶段训练框架 MemRU（Read SFT 学读取证据、Use GRPO 学利用证据）。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及视觉证据是否被模型真正利用这一 LVR 核心问题，其「读取失败 vs 使用失败」的拆解和分阶段监督可供核查视觉旁路、信息坍缩及训练信号分配对 latent 推理的启示。

title: EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
summary: Hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often arise from visual assumptions that go unchecked. Self-reflection, multi-agent debate, and counterfactual verification can reinforce erroneous conclusions when they rely on the same unverified visual assumptions. External visual tools can provide verifiable evidence, but models may select the wrong tools, supply incorrect parameters, or ignore or contradict the evidence they obtain. In this work, we propose EVA, an Evidence-seeking Visual Agent that reframes multimodal reasoning as an explicit process of evidence acquisition and verification. At the core of EVA is a unified evidence-grounded execution pipeline designed to address the above challenges through two tightly coupled mechanisms. First, we introduce Iterative Tool Replanning, which dynamically refines tool selection and parameters based on intermediate observations, improving the reliability of tool usage. Second, we develop Evidence Consistency Verification, an answer validation mechanism that improves alignment between the final prediction and the collected evidence, mitigating evidence--reasoning inconsistencies. In addition, to balance robustness and efficiency, EVA incorporates Selective Evidence Routing, an adaptive fast--slow reasoning strategy that determines when external evidence is necessary. Visually straightforward queries are handled via direct reasoning, while complex or high-risk cases trigger tool-based evidence acquisition. By jointly addressing how to reliably acquire evidence and how to use it consistently, EVA transforms multimodal reasoning from passive answer validation into explicit evidence-backed decision making. Experimental results demonstrate that EVA achieves significantly improved reasoning reliability over direct VLM inference and multi-agent methods, while maintaining efficiency through selective tool invocation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EVA 多模态智能体，把多模态推理重构为显式的视觉证据获取与验证流程：通过迭代式工具重规划修正工具选择与参数，用证据一致性验证对齐最终答案与已收集证据，并以选择性证据路由决定何时需要调用外部工具。
AI.relevance_reason: 与「获取证据、何时 LOOK、停止决策」直接相关，其证据筛选与答案—证据一致性检查或可用于核查 latent 内容是否真正被使用，以及外部视觉证据与内部推理状态冲突时的处理。

title: VTK-Bench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Distinguishing Language Priors and Text Modal Bias in Visual Language Models
summary: Visual language models (VLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities across various multimodal tasks, but they remain susceptible to hallucinations, undermining their reliability. Existing hallucination benchmarks primarily focus on identifying hallucinations and describing their manifestations, often neglecting their underlying causes. Specifically, multimodal hallucinations can stem from two distinct failure modes: text modality bias (TMB), reflecting an over-reliance on misleading text input; and language prior (LP), reflecting a reliance on previously learned knowledge. To differentiate these failure modes, we propose VTK-Bench, a benchmark that explicitly separates three information sources: visual information (V), textual information (T), and prior knowledge (K). By establishing mutually exclusive answers corresponding to V, T, and K, VTK-Bench enables fine-grained attribution analysis of model responses. Furthermore, we introduce discrete attribution and soft attribution metrics to characterize information source preferences. Extensive experiments on 11 representative open-source VLMs show that LP is more prevalent than TMB in most evaluated models. Notably, TMB decreases substantially with model scaling, whereas LP exhibits relatively limited improvement and remains the dominant failure mode. These findings highlight the importance of different information source preferences for a deeper understanding of multimodal hallucinations.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VTK-Bench，将信息源显式拆成视觉（V）、文本（T）与先验知识（K），为三者设计互斥答案，从而把 VLM 幻觉细粒度归因到文本模态偏置（TMB）或语言先验（LP），并给出离散与软归因指标；在 11 个开源 VLM 上发现 LP 更普遍，且随规模扩大 TMB 显著下降而 LP 改善有限。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「答案是否真正使用视觉证据」这一核心问题，可用于核查 LVR 回答是由内部视觉状态驱动还是被文本旁路与语言先验接管，其互斥答案设计与归因指标可供借鉴到 latent 贡献分配实验。

title: VAPOR: Improving Multimodal Reasoning with Sparse Visual Updates
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made substantial progress in visual reasoning, but extended generation over large visual contexts remains computationally expensive. During autoregressive decoding, visual attention is recomputed for every generated token, even when consecutive tokens rely on similar visual evidence. We introduce VAPOR (Visual Attention Persistence with On-demand Refresh), a training-free framework that reduces this redundancy by reusing visual attention outputs across decoding steps and refreshing them when needed. VAPOR caches the visual attention output while continuing to update textual attention at every step, helping reduce visual grounding drift during extended reasoning. To decide when to reuse cached outputs, VAPOR estimates visual attention mass using a low-rank approximation. It also uses prefill-based attention consistency and cache age to make independent Persist and Refresh decisions for each attention head. VAPOR retains the full visual key-value (KV) cache, so all visual tokens remain available when new evidence is needed. Experiments on eight image and four video reasoning benchmarks across two MLLM families show that VAPOR improves accuracy over dense attention on nearly all benchmarks while achieving 1.11-1.21x decoding speedups. Compared with the strongest state-of-the-art acceleration baseline in each setting, VAPOR further improves accuracy by 0.35-2.15 percentage points while achieving comparable or lower decoding latency. Our code is available at https://github.com/Su-my/VAPOR.

AI.brief_summary: VAPOR 提出一种免训练的解码加速框架：在自回归生成中复用视觉注意力输出，并利用低秩近似估计视觉注意力质量，结合 prefill 一致性与缓存年龄按注意力头决定继续复用还是刷新，同时保留完整视觉 KV cache。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接涉及多模态推理中视觉证据的按需获取与计算成本权衡，其逐头「persist/refresh」策略和视觉 grounding drift 分析，可能为 LVR 的 LOOK 决策、视觉证据筛选以及缓存和注意力结构对潜在状态的影响提供核查线索。

title: GlassGround: GUI Grounding Beyond Native Screenshots with Egocentric Wearable Vision
summary: Wearable assistants must localize interface elements from camera observations when direct screenshot access is unavailable, yet existing GUI grounding benchmarks primarily evaluate native screenshots. We introduce GlassGround, a new benchmark that pairs native screenshots with wearable camera observations while holding GUI states, instructions, and targets fixed. GlassGround contains 3,250 tasks across Android and iOS, captured using four wearable devices under four viewing conditions. Across ten open-source models, mean grounding accuracy drops from 94.8% on screenshots to 48.5% on camera images. Further analysis reveals that changes in target scale, screen geometry, and background cannot fully explain this performance degradation. We then study two ways to narrow this gap. At inference time, local zooming and screen rectification help but leave most of the gap. For training-time adaptation, we build on GlassGround's paired-view design and introduce PairDistill, a baseline that aligns target representations across views alongside coordinate supervision. Trained on independently collected data and using no screenshots at inference, it improves camera-image accuracy by 9.4 and 12.2 points on two backbones and transfers to unseen devices and operating systems. Combined with local zooming, it reaches 69.6% and 64.4%, but does not close the gap. The GlassGround dataset and code are available at https://github.com/yunnw/GlassGround.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GlassGround 基准，在固定 GUI 状态、指令与目标的前提下配对原生截图与四类可穿戴设备相机观测，发现十个开源模型平均定位准确率从 94.8% 降到 48.5%，并给出 PairDistill 跨视角目标表示对齐的训练基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其失败分析（缩放、几何、背景均无法完全解释退化）与跨视角表示对齐，直接触及 VLM 内部状态是否保留任务必要的视觉细节，可供核查视觉证据利用与「LOOK」阶段的表示对齐监督线索。

title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Immediate and Prospective Credit Assignment for Medical Visual Reasoning
summary: Medical visual question answering (VQA) requires acquiring useful evidence and deciding where to look next. Yet final-answer rewards do not reveal which observations support answering or guide subsequent inspection. We introduce MedPACT, an agentic reinforcement learning framework that learns selective observation policies through immediate answer support and prospective guidance. Our content-controlled estimator compares next actions induced by real and matched alternative observations under a shared real-observation history, isolating how observed content improves subsequent decisions. We combine both forms of credit within GRPO, assigning observation credit to the corresponding tool-call tokens alongside trajectory-level outcome supervision. MedPACT uses a single vision-language model and image-question-answer supervision, with credit estimation confined to training. Experiments with 4B and 8B backbones on six medical VQA benchmarks demonstrate improved accuracy, strong out-of-distribution generalization, and substantially lower inference costs. Case studies further illustrate how MedPACT avoids repeated observations and uses acquired evidence to guide subsequent inspection, demonstrating real-world practice potential.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MedPACT：一种面向医学视觉问答的 agentic RL 框架，用内容受控估计器把「即时答案支持」与「前瞻性引导」两类信用分配给观测类工具调用 token，并在 GRPO 中与轨迹级结果监督联合训练单一 VLM。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接研究视觉证据获取与「下一步看哪里」，并把信用精确落到观测动作上，与 LOOK 的收益—成本、证据筛选和贡献分配高度相关；其信用估计仅用于训练，可供核查推理期开销与停止决策是否被真正建模。

title: Can Its Own Misses Teach an MLLM to Find Small Brain Metastases?
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are becoming general readers of medical images, yet they remain weak at locating small abnormalities. Brain metastases expose this gap: at 384 px a 0.1 mL lesion covers less than a quarter of one visual token, and at one false positive per scan frontier MLLMs find fewer than 30% of lesions of 0.1-1 mL. Fine-tuning on one dataset helps but transfers poorly, and improving it further is slow trial and error steered by a single score. We introduce LANTERN (Lesion-finding AgeNt Through Error-driven Recursive learNing), a framework in which an MLLM improves recursively from its own misses. LANTERN recasts model development as an error-driven loop: a failure census attributes every missed lesion to one of four causes, an LLM mentor revises one of four levels (evidence acquisition, visual representation, learning policy, decision aggregation) per round, and a rule frozen before the first round decides what is kept, without test data and with every tool call audited. Over 15 unattended rounds, LANTERN raises a fine-tuned 4B MLLM from finding 75% to 94% of lesions at one false positive per scan on BraTS-MET, and 91% of those of 0.1-1 mL, compared with at most 51% and 29% for five frontier MLLMs read under the starting protocol; the gains hold on an external cohort (89%) and on unseen meningiomas (77%). These results show that an MLLM's own misses, attributed to their causes, can drive its reliable recursive self-improvement.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对 MLLM 难以定位极小脑转移灶的问题（0.1 mL 病灶不足四分之一个视觉 token），提出 LANTERN：将模型开发变成由自身漏检驱动的循环，先对漏检做四类归因，再由 LLM mentor 每轮修改证据获取、视觉表示、学习策略或决策聚合中的一层，并按预先冻结的规则保留改动。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉 token 容量限制 + 漏检归因 + 分级修改证据获取与视觉表示」直接对应 LVR 中对视觉细节是否进入内部状态、证据筛选与监督分配的关切，可供核查细粒度视觉信息在表示层面丢失的诊断方式。

title: The Missing Root: Geometric Imagination Without Images in Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes a new paradigm and method for giving large language models spatial understanding. Standard language models operate exclusively over discrete words (secondary representations of things rather than continuous space itself), forcing them to guess geometry verbally. Whereas most multimodal approaches equate spatial grounding with camera images or video frames, spatial structure itself is not a picture: it consists of coordinate frames, solid boundaries, and how objects move and relate to each other in continuous space. Motivated by this distinction, we place continuous object tokens combining pose (position, orientation, and scale) and signed-distance shape embeddings alongside word tokens inside a single uninterrupted transformer sequence, allowing language and geometry to attend to each other as object scenes are built and updated step by step. Control tokens switch output automatically between natural-language words and continuous object state updates to a persistent object workspace, while an attention mask blocks earlier prose when generating the answer, so responses must be read directly from settled geometry. To prove this method works, we attach a narrow parallel spatial stream (+4.4% weights) alongside unfrozen Qwen3-1.7B layers. In our two-dimensional tests, the model spawns and transforms multi-object scenes from English descriptions, transfers shapes to held-out nouns, and relies causally on the workspace to answer spatial questions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出让 LLM 在单一 transformer 序列中交错使用连续物体 token（位姿加符号距离形状嵌入）与词 token，并用控制 token 在自然语言输出与持续更新的物体工作区之间切换；在 Qwen3-1.7B 旁挂小型空间流，于二维场景验证从英文描述生成和变换多物体场景并回答空间问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应几何与任务必要信息能否保留在内部状态、答案是否真正读取 latent 内容；其生成答案时用注意力遮蔽阻断文本旁路、并以消融检验工作区因果作用的设计，可供核查 LVR 中的信息坍缩与旁路依赖。

title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
summary: Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. EATS constructs a memory of past interactions, including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback, and retrieves relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries. As memory construction does not require ground-truth supervision, EATS scales naturally with test-time experience. We evaluate EATS on tool-augmented medical reasoning tasks, including closed-ended visual question answering and free-form report generation. Experiments on four public datasets, ChestAgentBench, CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, and SLAKE-VQA, across three multimodal LLMs, Qwen3-VL 2B, Qwen3-VL 32B, and GPT-5.5, show consistent gains in tool selection behavior and downstream medical reasoning performance. Code is available at https://github.com/Limingyuan001/EATS.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EATS：为医学多模态推理智能体构建累积的工具使用经验记忆（查询、工具选择、参数与自评反馈），无需真值监督，在测试时检索相关经验以改进新查询的工具选择，并在四个数据集的视觉问答与报告生成任务上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「LOOK」一侧的证据获取决策：如何在不稳定的神经工具输出下选择调用哪个工具，其经验检索与自评反馈可供核查是否可支撑调用时机与停止判断；但论文不涉及 latent 推理状态与内部表示，联系限于工具选择层面。

title: RelPRM: Grounding Visual Process Reward Models in Relational Evidence
summary: Visual process reward models (PRMs) can detect calculation errors yet assign high scores to steps that misread visual relations. Supervision based on subsequent answer success does not directly establish whether a step's relational claim holds. To strengthen visual-relation verification, we first build an automated pipeline that programmatically verifies each claim and identifies the required objects, relations, and image regions. It produces RelProcessTrain and RelProcessBench (RPB), which tests whether scores respond appropriately to relational evidence through controlled image edits and step rephrasings. Building on this pipeline, we further introduce RelPRM, a visual-relation-oriented method for process reward modeling with two training mechanisms. Relation-evidence self-distillation constructs views preserving necessary objects, relations, and dependencies, reducing the burden of finding decisive evidence in complex scenes and transferring reliable evidence-assisted judgments to full images. Relation-evidence-driven consistency training encourages appropriate score changes when relation edits reverse a step's truth, stability under irrelevant edits, and similar score changes across paraphrases. At inference, RelPRM directly scores the current step using only the original image and reasoning context. RelPRM achieves 66.2% on VisualProcessBench (VPB) and 68.4% on RPB, gains of 4.2 and 9.9 percentage points over VisualPRM-8B. These results show that training for visual relations improves both relational verification and step assessment across broader multimodal reasoning tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建自动化流程程序化核验推理步骤中的视觉关系断言，产出 RelProcessTrain 与 RelProcessBench，并提出 RelPRM，以关系证据自蒸馏和关系编辑驱动的一致性训练，让过程奖励模型对关系证据而非仅答案成功敏感。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用受控图像编辑与步骤改写检验评分是否真正依赖视觉关系证据，与 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、步骤贡献分配与轨迹监督直接相关，可供核查以设计证据敏感的奖励或监督信号。

title: BayesPath: Reliability-Aware Bayesian Reasoning for Whole-Slide Pathology Agents
summary: Diagnosing whole-slide images (WSIs) requires hypothesis-driven reasoning: pathologists form a differential diagnosis, seek discriminative evidence, weigh its reliability, and stop once it suffices. However, existing training-free WSI agents lack an explicit framework for such reasoning. They typically use a large language model (LLM) to aggregate the region descriptions of a multimodal LLM (MLLM), without a belief over the candidates or regard for the descriptions' reliability. Consequently, a repeated model error counts as independent evidence for an incorrect diagnosis. We introduce BayesPath, a training-free WSI agent that casts the pathologist's Scan-Look-Weigh-Decide process as reliability-aware Bayesian reasoning. An explicit belief over the candidates is updated with each observation through a reliability-aware likelihood and guides where to look next and when to stop. This likelihood corrects for the models' answer bias, discounts correlated observations, and captures diagnostic confusions estimated without labels. The updates form an interpretable evidence trail of how each observation shapes the belief. On five MultiPathQA tasks spanning slide classification and slide VQA, BayesPath achieves the highest average accuracy among training-free agents, 58.6% against 34.1% for the next best, with large gains on slide classification. On identical observations, Bayesian updating outperforms LLM aggregation on average, even with a larger LLM. BayesPath's belief is also better calibrated than naive Bayes, so uncertain cases can be deferred to pathologists. Code is available at https://github.com/bryanwong17/BayesPath

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的全切片病理 agent BayesPath，将「扫描—观察—权衡—决策」建模为对候选诊断的显式贝叶斯信念更新：用可靠性感知似然（校正答案偏置、折扣相关观察、无标签估计混淆）决定下一步看哪里与何时停止，在五个 MultiPathQA 任务上取得免训练方法中最高平均准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 显式信念状态、观察可靠性与相关性折扣、停止判据直接对上 LVR 的视觉证据筛选与 LOOK/STOP 收益成本问题，且其非 latent 的概率式状态可作为 latent 工作区的对照基线，值得核查其去相关证据与标定评价方式是否可迁移。

title: When to Respond, Where to Ground: Streaming 3D Affordance Grounding
summary: Given a continuous RGB-D stream and a language request, streaming 3D affordance grounding requires an agent to decide when to respond and where to locate the requested functional part using only observations available so far. Existing 3D affordance grounding methods typically assume complete scene observations, while streaming vision-language models lack fine-grained 3D functional grounding. Our goal is to jointly determine response timing and functional-part localization during continuous scene observation. We propose StreamAff, an evidence-guided response strategy that makes both decisions from the grounding model's own visual evidence. The model scores the visual patches of the frames it reads: their combined support, weighed against a wait option, decides when to respond, and the highest-scoring patch selects the frame to ground in. A conditional look-back policy lets the model answer from an earlier observation at the moment of the request or wait for new evidence, and zoom-and-refine grounding segments the part named in the answer on the 3D points of the selected frame. We further introduce StreamFun3D, a benchmark derived from real-world 3D scenes that evaluates response timing and grounding across four evidence settings: Current, History, Future, and Unobserved, together with StreamIoU, a metric that credits a mask only when the response is timely and grounded in a valid source frame. We adapt offline 3D affordance grounding methods and build external-decider baselines that pair vision-language models with our mask decoder. StreamAff achieves 30.14% StreamIoU on 15-second streams, a 40.6% relative improvement over the strongest of these baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究流式 RGB-D 输入下的 3D affordance grounding，提出 StreamAff：用模型自身视觉 patch 的证据得分与「等待」选项比较来决定何时作答、选哪一帧定位，并配以回溯策略与 zoom-and-refine 分割；同时构建 StreamFun3D 基准与 StreamIoU 指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 以证据支持度对照「等待」选项来决定停止并选择证据来源帧，与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中的停止决策、视觉证据筛选高度对应，可供核查流式条件下的证据充分性判据；但未涉及内部 latent 推理状态，需注意其决策完全在输出层完成。

title: From Diagnosing Alignment to Joint Supervision in Multimodal Draft Training
summary: Multimodal drafts learn from multimodal (MM) and text-only (TXT) supervision, yet their effects on alignment and how to combine them remain unclear. We diagnose draft-target alignment through paired predictions with and without visual input, decomposing distributional error into text-conditioned and visual-response components. Drafts with similar text-conditioned alignment can still differ markedly in visual-response risk and acceptance. Controlled continuation training shows that high-risk groups outperform random and low-risk groups, and visual-response risk guides MM training more effectively than aggregate risk. Building on these diagnostics, we propose MNRS-Joint, which configures joint supervision from a given draft's component-risk distributions, using modality-specific mean risks to determine the MM:TXT mixture. Across three warm-ups, its distinct mixtures fall in high-performing regions of the ratio sweeps. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, MNRS-Joint improves mean accepted length from 3.35 to 3.53 and mean speedup from $2.04\times$ to $2.16\times$ over composition-matched random training under greedy tree decoding. The gains also hold under stochastic chain decoding.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断多模态 draft 模型的对齐：用带/不带视觉输入的配对预测把分布误差分解为文本条件与视觉响应两部分，发现文本对齐相近的 draft 在视觉响应风险与接受率上差异明显；据此提出 MNRS-Joint，按成分风险均值确定 MM:TXT 混合比例，在 LLaVA-1.5-7B 投机解码上把平均接受长度从 3.35 提到 3.53、加速比从 2.04× 提到 2.16×。
AI.relevance_reason: 带与不带视觉的配对预测可作为检测「视觉旁路」的现成诊断手段，成分风险分解与按风险配置监督配比的做法，可供核查能否迁移到 latent 推理中对视觉证据使用与训练贡献分配的度量。

title: What Makes a Gavagai? Learning Visual Concepts from One Positive and Few Negatives
summary: Humans can recognize novel concepts from only a few observations by identifying defining visual attributes and eliminating alternative interpretations. However, a single observation is consistent with multiple possible concepts, and accurate visual perception alone is insufficient to determine the intended interpretation. Negative evidence can reduce this ambiguity by eliminating competing hypotheses. Inspired by Quine's gavagai problem, we introduce the Gavagai Benchmark to evaluate whether vision-language models can identify the attributes defining a novel concept from positive and negative examples. The benchmark consists of synthetic images depicting novel combinations of visual attributes and real images of newly described species. Using these datasets, we examine how models use negative examples to identify novel concepts and analyze the respective roles of visual perception and reasoning. Several models struggle even when correct attributes are provided, while others show large gaps when ground-truth attributes are replaced with model predictions. These diagnostic comparisons highlight challenges in both attribute perception and inference from limited evidence.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Gavagai Benchmark，用合成属性组合图像与新描述物种的真实图像，考察视觉语言模型能否从单个正例和少量负例中识别界定新概念的关键视觉属性，并分别剖析视觉感知与推理的作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断基准直接触及内部状态是否保留任务必要视觉细节，以及负例如何消除竞争假设、筛选视觉证据；可与 LVR 中视觉旁路、信息坍缩和证据使用的问题对照，但研究本身不涉及 latent 推理状态，值得作为失败分析阅读。

title: Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding for Temporally Grounded Audio-Visual Understanding
summary: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) are designed to represent the temporal structure of audio and video, yet it remains unclear how effectively they use this temporal information to relate sounds to visual events. To examine this, we probe an AV-LLM on an audio-visual synchronization task by shifting the audio so that the queried sound overlaps a different visual event. We observe that the model still favors the originally aligned event over the newly aligned one, indicating limited sensitivity to changes in audio-visual temporal alignment. To address this, we propose Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding (MSCD), a training-free decoding method that emphasizes audio-visual temporal alignment in model predictions. MSCD contrasts logits under preserved and disrupted temporal alignment to favor predictions supported by aligned audio and video. We disrupt this alignment by temporally shifting either the audio or the video, while keeping the other modality fixed. Extensive evaluations with two AV-LLMs across three benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of MSCD for temporally grounded audio-visual understanding. In particular, MSCD improves accuracy over the base models on Daily-Omni by 2.2 and 2.8 percentage points for OmniVinci and video-SALMONN 2+, respectively, suggesting that emphasizing temporal alignment can also benefit broader audio-visual understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 论文通过时间平移音频、制造音视频事件错位，检验 AV-LLM 是否真正依据跨模态时间对齐作答，并提出免训练对比解码 MSCD，对比对齐与破坏对齐时的 logits 以强化时间一致的预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接触及多模态推理是否使用时间证据与模态对齐信息，而非依赖表面捷径；其对齐扰动与解码期证据筛选思路可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据使用和贡献分配问题。

title: Can Visual World Models See Force?
summary: World models and vision-language-action policy models are increasingly proposed as foundations for robot manipulation. They predict how scenes evolve and which actions to take, yet successful manipulation depends not solely on following observable trajectories but also on the hidden variable of interaction force. Neurophysiology has shown that humans possess a visual prior for this hidden variable, motivating us to ask the question: Do the representations of visual foundation models also capture the forces involved in an interaction? We define force awareness as the ability of representations to (1) indicate when contact force is applied, (2) track how it changes during an interaction, and (3) reflect how large it is. We probe frozen image, video, world- and policy model representations with a lightweight readout trained on synchronized video and force measurements from two manipulation datasets. Our experiments show that most models capture when contact occurs but not how much force is being applied. Surprisingly, robot post-training does not improve this either, highlighting an important gap in current models capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出「力感知」的三项判据（是否发生接触、力如何变化、力有多大），用轻量 readout 探测冻结的图像、视频、世界模型与策略模型表征能否编码交互力这一隐变量。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于对多模态内部状态是否保留任务必要（视觉不可直接观测）信息的表示诊断，其「能察觉接触却难以量化力度、机器人后训练也无改善」的结论可与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、latent 内容与深度/位置效应的解读对照。

title: Evidence-Aligned Benchmarking and Learning for Medical Video Language Models
summary: A medical video language model should answer from the visual evidence its question asks about. We find three places where this breaks down and address each with an approach we call MedEvidU. First, benchmarks reward answers that ignore the video: on one dataset, the position of a clip within its recording predicts the surgical step in 37% of questions, and a constant answer beats every trained model on a standard safety-assessment metric. We build MedVidBench-v2, 34 tasks from 18 surgical and clinical video datasets, in which prompts and metrics are audited with answers given without video, and which tests unseen hospitals and windows cut blindly from whole recordings. Second, common video encoders merge consecutive frames into shared tokens, so a question about one frame is answered from a blend of two. Query-slot inputs give each queried frame its own tokens at almost no extra cost. Third, a fine-tuned model has memorized its training questions, which leaves little to learn from. Label-matched question resampling (LQR) adds unseen questions about the same recordings while keeping the answer distribution fixed, in a final supervised epoch and in reinforcement learning. Together, these raise the grounding IoU of a 4B model from 30.4 to 44.4, above a supervised 27B model, and instrument grounding at an unseen hospital from 33.9 to 72.5. On blindly cut windows, event-presence accuracy improves by 5.5 points and localization F1 by 8.1 points. Project page: https://gaozhongpai.github.io/MedEvidU/

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对医学视频语言模型答非所视的问题提出 MedEvidU：构建经「无视频作答」审计的基准 MedVidBench-v2，用 query-slot 让被问帧独占 token，并以标签匹配问题重采样减少记忆，从而提升视觉证据定位与跨医院泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其诊断的三类失效——位置先验与恒定答案即可刷分、帧间 token 合并使证据混杂、微调后只记住训练问题——正对应 LVR 关注的视觉旁路、内部状态信息坍缩与证据筛选，基准审计与逐帧 token 设计可供核查借鉴。

title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
summary: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior digital actions remain valid. Whether current agents can reliably handle these changes remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce EgoUseBench, a benchmark for evaluating Ego Use across three interaction settings with different levels of first-person context. Computer-Use relies on explicit instructions, Offline Ego Use provides prerecorded first-person context before execution, and Online Ego Use provides continuous observations as user intent evolves. Based on over 74 hours of real-world first-person recordings, we construct 693 tasks across the three interaction settings. To capture task evolution, we track first-person observations, user requirements, and website state separately. We further group tasks by how information changes during execution, resulting in three types: Graft (revised user requirements), Refresh (new first-person observations), and Clarify (agent-initiated information seeking). We evaluate advanced models and find that average success rates in Online Ego Use are 26.3% lower than in Computer-Use. This result reveals the difficulty of keeping task execution aligned with evolving first-person context and user intent.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EgoUseBench，基于 74 小时真实第一人称录像构建 693 个任务，在 Computer-Use、离线与在线 Ego Use 三种设置下评估计算机使用智能体能否随第一人称观察和用户意图变化而修正理解与操作。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准直接考察多模态智能体如何筛选持续到达的视觉证据、修正意图理解并决定是否重新寻求信息，与 LVR 中的证据获取、状态更新及 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本问题联系明确，可供核查。

title: Decoder-as-a-Probe: Verbalizing and Steering Visual Representations in LVLMs
summary: It is commonly accepted that high-level concepts are represented linearly in the representation space of large neural networks. For Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs), finding those interpretable directions in visual representations is important for interpretability. To find them, the classical approach is to train a linear classifier on the representations, but it needs a large amount of labels and only recovers what can be read from the representations, not what the model actually uses. In this paper we start from the following insight: The LLM Decoder of an LVLM is also a classifier whose classes are the possible next tokens. So we use its first-order Taylor expansion as a linear classifier. Hence, we introduce Decoder-as-a-Probe (DaP), which significantly outperforms classical probing and steering baselines especially when training data is sparse. (1) It verbalizes what an LVLM perceives in a given image. (2) It can surgically change the perception of the LVLM about specific attributes (e.g. change only the color, the clothes worn or the action done). Due to its simplicity and data efficiency, we believe DaP can serve as a plug-and-play tool for LVLM research, such as interpretability, hallucination mitigation or instruction tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Decoder-as-a-Probe（DaP），把 LVLM 的 LLM decoder 一阶 Taylor 展开当作线性分类器，用于读出图像视觉表征并定向修改颜色、衣着、动作等属性感知，在标注稀疏时优于传统 probing 与 steering 基线。

title: Recalling the Past to Answer the Present: Context-Aware Multi-Evidence Reasoning for Streaming Video Question Answering
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in video understanding, yet existing video question answering (VQA) benchmarks mainly evaluate models in offline settings. Real-world streaming scenarios instead require models to answer context-dependent queries by retrieving and reasoning over evidence distributed across the video history. We introduce StreamRecall, a benchmark for context-aware Multi evidence reasoning in streaming video QA. StreamRecall requires models to retrieve, associate, and reason over temporally scattered evidence to answer queries at the appropriate moment. It contains 4,983 questions over 462 videos, with context-aligned query times and fine-grained temporal evidence annotations. We further propose the Evidence Utilization Cascade to diagnose model reasoning through evidence localization, grounding, chain completion, and answer derivation. To enable efficient long-term streaming reasoning, we present EviStream, a training-free causal visual memory mechanism that preserves reasoning-critical evidence under a fixed KV budget. Experiments reveal substantial gaps between current VLMs and realistic streaming requirements, establishing StreamRecall as a foundation for developing evidence-aware streaming video intelligence.

title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
summary: Answering a knowledge-based visual question requires first recognizing the entity in the image and then recalling knowledge about it. Thinking vision-language models (VLMs) reason for thousands of tokens before answering, yet it remains underexplored how well such thinking VLMs perform each of these two steps. We therefore analyze thinking VLMs on this task and make two key observations. (1) Recognition is the bottleneck, since 76.3% of errors across four models on ViQuAE stem from misrecognizing the entity, and 84.9% of these failures are resolved once the entity name is provided in the question. (2) Recognition is driven by entity-recall clues rather than by general descriptions of the image. An entity-recall clue is a distinctive visual detail that helps the model recall the entity, such as keys, a traditional attribute of Saint Peter. Based on these findings, we propose ClueRL, a reinforcement learning approach that extends Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with an advantage localized to the entity-recall clue in the thinking trace. Rather than injecting new entity knowledge, ClueRL changes how VLMs think: it leads them to attend more closely to visual details and spot these clues, helping them use the knowledge they already have. Consequently, it outperforms both GRPO and a perception-reward baseline on three entity recognition benchmarks. Moreover, this clue-seeking behavior generalizes beyond entity recognition, the only task used for training. Since recognition is the bottleneck, the gains carry over to knowledge-based visual question answering. They even extend to general multimodal reasoning, raising Qwen3.5-4B by 4.4 and 4.0 points on the ScienceQA and MMMU subsets of MMStar, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文拆解知识型视觉问答为「先识别实体、再回忆知识」两步，发现 thinking VLM 的错误主要源于实体识别失败，且识别依赖「实体回忆线索」这类独特视觉细节而非整体场景描述；据此提出 ClueRL，在 GRPO 中把优势定位到思考轨迹里的线索片段，引导模型关注细节、用已有知识作答，并在实体识别、知识型 VQA 与通用多模态推理上取得提升。

title: Seeing the Right Context: Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Remote Sensing
summary: Remote sensing scene understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to interpret queried targets in relation to nearby objects and surrounding structures, which serve as spatial references or define the scope of an answer. However, standard answers and bounding boxes often leave these contextual relationships implicit. Thus, we construct GeoContext-5K to make them explicit in 5,394 training pairs for visual question answering (VQA), with spatial cues, visual facts, and supporting regions. GeOPD uses these annotations for on-policy distillation, guiding a frozen teacher with region marks on the full image and a visual fact while preserving surrounding spatial references. It prioritizes teacher corrections that agree with the shift in the student's next token distribution when evidence is restored. A complementary objective weights the contrast between the student's scores on the two views by how much masking lowers the teacher's log probability for the same sampled token. Experiments on five remote sensing VQA benchmarks show that GeOPD outperforms the evaluated open-source MLLMs and matched post-training baselines, improving over the 4B and 9B base models by 5.81 and 2.97 percentage points on average. The dataset and code will be publicly released at https://github.com/YeeCharm/GeOPD.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文构建 GeoContext-5K 遥感 VQA 数据集，用显式空间线索、视觉事实与支撑区域标注，并据此设计 GeOPD 的 on-policy 蒸馏，让冻结教师通过区域标记和视觉事实提供纠正信号，在五个遥感 VQA 基准上优于开源 MLLM 与匹配的后训练基线。

title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
summary: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. We therefore pose the same tasks, with identical inputs, output specification and evaluator, to both media: rather than denoising pixels, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video, which an unmodified rule-based evaluator scores. On VBVR-Pro-Bench (Xu et al., 2026), a 500-instance suite spanning five cognitive categories with symbolic ground truth, the agent receives the same first frame and prompt as the video model, with no access to ground truth, metadata or generation models, and one attempt per instance. Three closed-model agents (Codex with gpt-6-astra, Claude Code with Fable 5.1 and Gemini CLI with Gemini 3.1 Pro) score 0.923, 0.894 and 0.893, each more than 0.22 above the strongest video model. Among 23 runnable open-weight models, the best, GLM-5, reaches 0.572, above all video models except the RL-trained one. Together, we show that for tasks whose solutions can be computed from a first frame and a prompt, program synthesis is currently a substantially more reliable route to visual reasoning than video generation. We further distinguish depictive programs, which navigate the image to recover a transferable scheme, from propositional programs, which operate on hard-coded values, revealing how visual reasoning unfolds in agent-written programs and what it implies for its nature of reasoning in general.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 VBVR-Pro-Bench 上用相同首帧、提示与评测器，对比视频生成模型与 coding agent 编写渲染程序两条路线，发现三个闭源 agent 得分均高出最强视频模型 0.22 以上，并区分「描绘式」与「命题式」程序以刻画视觉推理如何在代码中展开。

title: Stranger Things: When Objects Appear Without Their Typical Neighbors
comment: This paper was accepted to the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Track on Evaluations and Datasets. Dataset: huggingface.co/datasets/sidgairo18/strange-bench
summary: Visual context is a powerful cue for object recognition: scenes inform what, where, and at what scale objects are likely to appear. Yet over-reliance on context becomes a failure mode when models predict objects based on their typical neighbors rather than the objects' own visual features, which we call typicality bias. While extensively studied in the pre-Transformer era, it has often been assumed that architectural and scale improvements would naturally solve it, and a systematic diagnostic across the modern vision stack remains absent. We provide such a diagnostic framework. We measure typicality bias via normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI) over object pairs, and introduce STRANGE-Bench (Synthetic Typicality-RANked Grounded Evaluation Benchmark): a photorealistic, layout-controlled benchmark spanning 17 sub-tiers from typical to never-co-occurring object pairs. Across five model families (specialist detectors, open-vocabulary detectors, self-supervised, vision-language, and multimodal large language models) and three recognition tasks (supervised detection, open-vocabulary detection, and classification), the bias is prevalent: gaps of 5-11 p.p. persist when objects appear outside their typical company, and do not consistently shrink with scale. To mitigate it, we turn to data augmentation: existing augmentations are designed for visual diversity, not for breaking co-occurrence shortcuts, and sample from the very distribution that produces typicality bias. We propose Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS), a simple sampling rule for paste-based augmentations that uses the NPMI signal to tilt the training-time co-occurrence distribution toward atypical partners. AAS reduces the typicality gap by up to 1.6 p.p. on natural-image COCO splits and 23.0 p.p. on synthetic STRANGE-Bench across three model families, without sacrificing overall performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用 NPMI 量化物体对共现典型性，构建布局可控、分 17 个典型性档位的 STRANGE-Bench，在检测、开放词表检测与分类任务上考察五类模型（含 VLM 与 MLLM）的「典型性偏差」，并提出按 NPMI 调整粘贴式增强共现分布的 Anchor-Atypicality Sampling 以缓解该偏差。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接追问模型是依据物体自身视觉特征还是共现先验作答，与 LVR 关心的「答案是否真正使用视觉证据、是否出现视觉旁路」相通；其 NPMI 分层基准与 AAS 采样可供核查为检验 latent 状态视觉依赖性的评价与训练线索。

title: ProbFaS: Probabilistic Video Frame Selection for MLLMs via Multi-Fidelity Calibration
summary: Processing long videos with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is prohibitively expensive, making informative frame selection essential for accurate video understanding. The default uniform sampling often misses task-relevant keyframes, while recent training-free selectors instead pick frames by how well each one matches the question under an image-text alignment (ITA) score. However, we show that ITA signals correspond poorly with the MLLM's true needs: their rankings correlate weakly with downstream accuracy and are even negatively correlated on over 40% of questions, whereas the MLLM's internal yes/no judgment yields a much stronger signal. We present ProbFaS, a training- and label-free probabilistic pipeline that fuses both signals for key frame selection. ProbFaS treats dense ITA scores as cheap, biased measurements and sparse MLLM judgments as accurate, costly ones, unifying them via co-kriging, a multi-fidelity Gaussian process, to calibrate relevance across all frames. A temporal determinantal point process then selects frames capturing relevance peaks while preserving temporal coverage. Across Video-MME, MLVU and LongVideoBench, ProbFaS is the most accurate among fourteen state-of-the-art training-free selectors and uniform sampling in 13 of 15 settings (8-128 frames), outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 3.1 percentage points. On MLVU and LongVideoBench, 32 ProbFaS frames match or surpass the top baseline at 128 frames and uniform sampling with up to 768 frames.

AI.brief_summary: 针对长视频 MLLM 的帧选择，作者指出图文对齐（ITA）分数与下游准确率仅弱相关、甚至在四成问题上负相关，MLLM 内部 yes/no 判断信号更强，于是提出免训练免标签的 ProbFaS：用 multi-fidelity 高斯过程（co-kriging）把稠密廉价的 ITA 分数与稀疏昂贵的 MLLM 判断融合，再用时序 DPP 选帧。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及「看哪里」的视觉证据筛选及廉价/昂贵证据采集的成本权衡，并给出「图文相似度不等于模型真正所需证据」的诊断，可为 LVR 中证据筛选与用模型自身判断校准相关性提供核查线索。

title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
summary: A general-purpose Vision-Language Model (VLM) has surpassed expert vision models in many domains such as object detection and video recognition. However, point correspondence is known to be challenging for VLMs since it goes beyond object-level recognition: it requires pixel-level localization of the same physical surface point across observations, even when appearance changes or the point disappears and later reappears. In this paper, we introduce AgenTAP, a VLM-based agent that directly predicts point coordinates and visibility and actively reasons over videos. Starting from its own estimate, the agent autonomously chooses what to inspect and uses the resulting evidence to verify point identity and refine its predictions. With GPT-6 Astra, it surpasses expert vision models in both point localization and visibility prediction, without correspondence-specific fine-tuning. We further use AgenTAP to re-identify physical points after disappearance and reconnect fragmented tracks, constructing EgoTAP-4D, a dataset of 3D point trajectories in long real-world egocentric videos. On sampled reappearing points, its predictions approach human agreement, and adding EgoTAP-4D to D4RT training improves average 3D tracking performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AgenTAP，让通用 VLM 以 agent 方式做点对应：从自身估计出发主动决定查看何处，用获得的视觉证据核验点的身份并迭代修正坐标与可见性预测，还借助它重识别消失后的点并构建长视频 3D 点轨迹数据集 EgoTAP-4D。

title: Confidence-Based Adaptive Retrieval Fails Where It Matters Most: A Paradox in Biomedical Question Answering
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for biomedical question answering, but plausible incorrect answers remain a safety risk in clinical settings. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can ground responses in medical literature, while confidence-based adaptive RAG retrieves only when the model appears uncertain. We evaluate this routing strategy on three biomedical QA benchmarks of increasing difficulty and compare models across a broad range of parameter scales. The results reveal a paradox: confidence is well calibrated (AUROC 0.78--0.89) on standard medical exam questions where retrieval adds little value (+2.4\% to -1.4\%), yet becomes \emph{near-random} (AUROC 0.506) on specialist-level questions where retrieval helps most (+11.2\%). Five uncertainty signals---first-token probability, margin, entropy, consistency-based sampling, and verbalized confidence---show the same failure pattern. Five post-hoc calibration correction strategies, including density-ratio reweighting and rank-preserving transformation, do not recover a useful routing signal on hard questions (best AUROC: 0.507). Cross-model comparison shows that larger parameter scale and higher base accuracy do not guarantee reliable confidence-based routing under specialist-domain difficulty shift. These findings challenge the premise of confidence-based adaptive RAG: in high-stakes biomedical settings, defaulting to always-retrieve is safer and more accurate than confidence-based routing when calibration on the target domain is unknown.

AI.brief_summary: 在三个难度递增的生物医学 QA 基准上评估「仅当模型不确定时才检索」的置信度自适应 RAG 路由，覆盖多种参数规模与五种不确定性信号、五种事后校准修正，发现置信度在简单考题上校准良好但检索收益有限，在专家级难题上接近随机（AUROC 0.506）而检索收益最大。
AI.relevance_reason: 「置信度门控何时检索」与 LVR 中「何时 LOOK、是否追加视觉证据」的决策机制同构，其「难题上自评信号失效、修正无效」的结论可供核查 latent 自评与停止信号是否也存在同样的难度偏移与校准陷阱。

title: Two Timescales of Forgetting in Fine-tuning of Language Models: Fast Behavioral Suppression and Slow Representational Drift
summary: Today, a core pipeline of artificial intelligence systems is pretraining on a broad range of text corpora and then fine-tuning on specific tasks or desired behaviors. Yet we still have limited understanding of how fine-tuning on a restricted data distribution modifies representations acquired during pretraining. In particular, it remains unclear whether surface behavioral suppression happens together with the erasure of latent representations that support it. In this work, we study supervised fine-tuning (SFT) by pretraining transformers on a controlled context-free grammar with hierarchical latent structure, the Random Hierarchy Model (RHM), and fine-tuning with a restricted subset of its generative rules. While during pretraining the model's ability to generate with the correct grammar rules coincides with building the internal representations of the corresponding latent, we find that SFT exhibits a very different dynamics: (i) the generation of deleted rules changes on a fast timescale inversely proportional to the magnitude of the token-latent correlation; meanwhile, their corresponding representations stay intact; (ii) the hidden representations of the deleted rules become forgotten on a much longer timescale, associated with a slow drift of the network parameters. Finally, we observe analogous results in a realistic setup with natural language, suggesting that this timescale separation in forgetting is a more general phenomenon of fine-tuning language models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在受控文法预训练加受限规则监督微调的设定及自然语言实验中，发现被删除规则的生成能力快速下降，而对应隐表示暂时保留、随后才在更长时间尺度上随参数漂移而被遗忘。

title: What Does RL Post-Training Teach Text-to-Image Models? A Skill-Wise Analysis of Flow-GRPO
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become a standard way to improve text-to-image flow models: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, a gain read as the model having learned compositional generation. We ask how much of that gain the base model's own samples already contained, by measuring pass@k over shared noise seeds, one skill at a time, before and after RL, on prompts never used in training. The answer differs by skill. On four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening: one post-trained sample is worth 4 to 10 base samples, and pass@32 barely moves. On spatial relations it is unlocking: pass@32 rises from 0.69 to 1.00, 128 base samples do not match one post-trained sample, and prompts the base model never solved in 32 samples are solved 93% of the time, as often as those it solved. The benchmark average, 31 base samples per post-trained sample, describes no skill. Relations carry 35% of the gain; of the other 65%, selecting among 8 base samples with the judge behind the reward recovers nine tenths. We propose an account of when each occurs: within a prompt, a group-relative update re-weights only the outcomes its samples contain, and a flow policy cannot widen the noise that produces them; across prompts, shared parameters let successes on some prompts repair a deficit common to many. The same anatomy applies to a text-rendering checkpoint. The account's predictions are tested with a checkpoint trained without KL, within-prompt diversity, and controlled training that holds object classes out, where sharpening comes first and transfers, and unlocking follows, on practised objects before unseen ones.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在共享噪声种子上分技能测 pass@k，比较 Flow-GRPO 前后表现，把 RL 增益拆成「锐化」（重加权基模型已有解）与「解锁」（如空间关系），并给出机制解释与预测验证。

title: State Space Attention: Learning Context-Dependent Memory Retention
summary: Standard attention's key-value cache grows linearly with context length. Bounding it raises the question of what a sequence model should retain for long-context reasoning. We argue this choice should be learned, and introduce State Space Attention (SSA), which learns to keep a bounded set of past representations and reads them with standard attention. A learned scorer rescores every chunk against newly arriving context and the rest of memory. A fixed-context Transformer is then the special case that always keeps the most recent tokens. We train the scorer and reader jointly, either moving gradually from a differentiable soft weighting of memories to hard retention, or with hard retention from the start. To produce signal for the scorer, we generate supervised samples during training, a technique we call recovery. We compare SSA with recurrent models, bounded-memory attention methods, and full-attention Transformers across retrieval, variable tracking, multi-hop reasoning, and language modeling. On our retrieval and reasoning benchmarks, SSA matches or comes within a few points of full attention on most tasks, far outperforms a Transformer with the same readable budget on every long-context retrieval task we evaluate, and matches or outperforms one with about 4 times that budget, while using constant inference memory. The largest remaining gap to full attention at small language model scale is on RULER. SSA makes a fixed number of tokens useful over a longer context, and since it reads memory with standard attention, we propose that it can be stacked with KV cache eviction methods. We also pretrain and post-train 400M-parameter models and measure how SSA's training and inference costs scale with context length and model size. Together, these experiments examine the capabilities and limitations of learned memory retention for long-context sequence modeling.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 State Space Attention：用一个可学习打分器对历史表示块反复重新打分，保留有界记忆并用标准 attention 读取，从软加权逐步过渡到硬保留，并借助训练期「recovery」监督信号训练打分器，在长上下文检索与推理任务上接近全注意力且推理内存恒定。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本长上下文工作，但其「学什么该留、按新上下文重估旧状态」的保留机制与 recovery 式监督，可能为 LVR 中的 latent 状态更新、记忆筛选与轨迹监督提供可核查线索。

title: PRIOR: Pre-Call Reasoning in SFT and Its Influence on Tool-Use Retention under RL
summary: Tool use learned during supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is not always retained during reinforcement learning (RL). We study how properties of SFT data may affect this retention by constructing Low, Medium, and High SFT datasets with approximately matched token budgets but different tool-call depths. Under the same RL recipe, the three initializations reach similar RL training accuracy yet exhibit markedly different tool-use dynamics: tool initiation increases in Low, declines in Medium, and collapses in High. We observe that these datasets also differ substantially in the amount of reasoning preceding each tool call. In particular, High trajectories contain considerably less pre-call reasoning, motivating the hypothesis that pre-call reasoning may affect how well tool use is calibrated and, consequently, whether the corresponding behaviors are retained during RL. An idealized theoretical analysis provides a selective-retention view of this process: advantages in overall and tool-conditioned accuracy can be preserved under outcome-only optimization, while tool initiation increases only when tool-using trajectories are more successful than the tool-free alternative. Guided by this analysis, we rank the original High trajectories by average pre-call reasoning length and retain the highest-ranked examples while approximately matching cumulative SFT token exposure. This simple filtering strategy improves post-RL accuracy and tool-conditioned final-answer success without consistently increasing tool initiation across multiple benchmarks. These results suggest that pre-call reasoning is a useful dimension of SFT supervision for understanding and improving tool-use retention under downstream RL.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文考察 SFT 数据中工具调用深度与「调用前推理」量的差异如何影响 RL 阶段工具使用的保留：构造 token 预算相近但调用深度为低/中/高的数据集，观察到 RL 后工具启动分别上升、下降和崩溃，并给出一套选择性保留的理论解释，进而按平均 pre-call 推理长度筛选高深度样本以改善 RL 后准确率与工具条件下成功率。

title: Where to Approximate: Understanding and Accelerating Looped Multi-View Reconstruction
summary: Looped multi-view reconstruction refines scene features by repeatedly applying a shared transformer block. Making these updates cheaper requires knowing how an approximation at one step affects the rest of the refinement. We study this with paired interventions in Déjà View and stacked reconstruction transformers, separating the error an approximation injects, how that error propagates, and how it affects the output. In Déjà View, approximation errors are attenuated more strongly than matched random perturbations under a scale-adjusted state-error measure, and a local Jacobian decomposition separates the contribution of channel gating from the response to spatial error structure. Spatial approximations made early benefit from subsequent refinement, whereas cross-step reuse depends on which quantity is cached and how reuse steps are spaced. At equal final norm, approximation errors change the predicted rotations 1.55 times as much as random errors. These findings guide our proposed method, which reduces spatial resolution and pools keys and values early in refinement, then interleaves attention-output reuse with full attention, and is adapted through lightweight self-distillation. Across five reconstruction benchmarks, the balanced configuration runs $1.63\times$ faster than the official 16-step Déjà View model with a 1.86-point reduction in average pose AUC@$3^\circ$. At matched latency, it exceeds the interpolated curve of a trained baseline using full refinement blocks by 4.73 points in AUC@$3^\circ$ and improves the corresponding geometry metrics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究循环多视图重建中近似误差如何被注入、传播并影响输出，通过配对干预与局部 Jacobian 分解区分误差来源，并据此提出早期降分辨率、KV 池化、注意力输出复用与轻量自蒸馏的加速方案。

title: DLaR: Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: Latent reasoning enables LLMs to operate in continuous embedding space, yet existing methods suffer from deterministic inference that precludes exploration of diverse reasoning paths. While recent approaches inject stochasticity to restore exploration, we identify two fundamental limitations: \textit{uniform stochasticity} across all steps is suboptimal, and unconstrained perturbations disrupt reasoning coherence. We propose Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning (DLaR), a framework with two complementary mechanisms that operate at different temporal granularities within the GRPO reinforcement learning framework. At the token level, Adaptive Stochasticity Modulation (ASM) dynamically adjusts perturbation intensity at each latent step based on a confidence-entropy fusion signal, increasing exploration when the model is uncertain and preserving stability when confident. At the training level, Training-Aware Stochasticity Tuning (TAST) progressively decays the base stochasticity level following a curriculum schedule. Through this dual-level design, DLaR establishes a hierarchical exploration-exploitation strategy that operates at both token and training levels. Extensive experiments on four in-distribution and three out-of-distribution mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DLaR achieves the highest average performance across model scales, reaching 27.9%/50.6% Pass@1/Pass@8 on Llama-3.2-1B and 46.8%/68.2% on Qwen2.5-1.5B. Code: \href{https://github.com/xiaocen-luo/DLaR}{https://github.com/xiaocen-luo/DLaR}.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DLaR，在 GRPO 框架下对 latent reasoning 的随机性做动态控制：token 级用置信度-熵融合信号自适应调节每步扰动强度，训练级按课程逐步衰减基础随机性，从而形成分层探索-利用策略，并在数学推理基准上验证。

title: When Position Favors the Wrong Part: Evaluating Left-Right Discrimination in Semantic Correspondence
summary: Overall part-discrimination accuracy can conceal failures when image position favors the wrong bilateral part. We examine whether dense descriptors distinguish the correct part under this conflict and whether their discrimination scores help select matching coordinates. We evaluate position agreement and conflict within the same target images and annotated part pairs, using a bounding-box-side score to define the conditions. We compare the original descriptors with their even and odd components under horizontal reflection, examine feature upsampling with the backbone and adapters fixed, and test candidate-selection rules based on odd scores. On SPair-71k, odd discrimination accuracy falls from 86.66% under agreement to 19.63% under conflict for frozen DINOv2, compared with 95.27% to 86.16% for MARCO. With MARCO's input geometry fixed, odd accuracy in box-side conflict was 34.12% on the native grid and 88.84% after learned upsampling and pooling back to that grid. Odd-score rules improve on the original hard-peak matchers overall for DINOv2 and DINOv3 and on conflict queries for MARCO. With MARCO's soft decoder fixed, reranking the cosine peaks changes mean per-pair PCK by +0.47 pp. For supervised GeoAware-SC, using the odd score to select the localization window center yields only 15 net additional correct matches, with 330 corrections and 315 introduced errors. Evaluating discrimination under position conflict reveals failures hidden by aggregate accuracy. Reporting corrections and introduced errors separately also shows whether a discriminative score produces useful matching decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在语义对应任务上构造位置一致与位置冲突两种条件，用包围盒侧别得分衡量 dense descriptor（DINOv2、MARCO、GeoAware-SC）能否区分正确的左右部件，并检验冻结骨干下的特征上采样以及基于水平反射奇偶分量得分的候选筛选规则。

title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
summary: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, \emph{model-driven} context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models that use the context API effectively reach higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets: \textbf{GPT 6.1 nearly triples its score at a 32K budget} on OfficeQA Pro v2 (21\%~$\rightarrow$~56\%), and \textbf{Kimi gains with up to 41\% fewer input tokens}. Models differ widely, however, in how often they use the API, how aggressively they compact, and when they start compacting, and prompt changes shift that timing. Finally, we show that \textbf{inference engines can make model-driven edits cheaper}: by reusing the KV cache of the unchanged suffix after an edit, \textbf{we cut prefill compute by up to 15\% per request with no measurable change in accuracy}. Together, these results point to a new co-design frontier: models trained to manage their own context, served by inference engines that support KV cache editing.
