title: The Geometry Is the Memory: Task-Density Routing for Continual LoRA
summary: Freezing older adapters does not ensure that a continual learner will select and use them properly at inference time. When multiple adapters exist, routing among them and identifying the adapter whose representation space matches the query's answer can be difficult. We propose CONTLORA, which replaces stored examples with compact class statistics for adapter selection and classification. Gaussian class models in a frozen representation select LoRA adapters, while accumulated feature moments exactly recover a class-balanced ridge classifier for fixed training features. Trained without retaining images or feature vectors, CONTLORA reaches 88.55% accuracy on 20-task CIFAR-100 and 86.99% on CUB-200. Across three benchmarks in the matched component study, its mean final accuracy differs from an independently trained stored-feature counterpart by at most 0.07 percentage points. Ablations show that improved task coverage need not improve classification and adapter composition also matters. On held-out classes, competitor-centered likelihood scores improve novelty AUROC over raw likelihood without altering routing ranks. These results support statistical memory as an alternative to example-retention approaches in the evaluated settings, while identifying task ambiguity as an ongoing limitation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CONTLORA，用冻结表示中的紧凑类别统计与高斯类模型选择 LoRA 适配器，并以累积特征矩精确恢复类平衡岭分类器，在不保存样例的情况下完成持续图像分类。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按表示空间匹配度路由和组合适配器、并用似然分数判别新类的做法，可能为 LVR 的工作区选择、模块路由与证据筛选提供方法线索，但未涉及多模态推理，可迁移性需核查。

title: CA-RAG: Constraint-Aligned Retrieval for Structurally Faithful Long-Form Generation
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. Semantically relevant retrieval may therefore omit information needed for mandatory downstream clauses. We propose Constraint-Aligned RAG (CA-RAG), a retrieval-conditioning framework that augments section-specific queries with ontology-derived structural constraints and policy-grounded knowledge-graph relations before evidence selection. Retrieval-only evaluation with manually annotated evidence shows consistent improvements across retrieval budgets. At $k=6$, CA-RAG increases Precision@$k$ from $0.5268$ to $0.5692$, pooled Recall@$k$ from $0.5402$ to $0.5950$, and F1@$k$ from $0.5389$ to $0.5672$ over standard RAG. Generation experiments further show improvements in compliance and reliability in several model--domain settings, while generation-only constraints achieve higher clause coverage but lower overall compliance and reliability. These results indicate that structurally aligned retrieval can improve evidence sufficiency in compliance-sensitive long-form generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CA-RAG，在检索前用本体导出的结构约束与政策知识图谱关系改写分节查询，使证据选择对齐合规长文生成的强制性条款要求，并在检索与生成层面评估其效果。

title: A Perturbation-Driven Framework for Sensitivity Analysis of Dimensionality Reduction
comment: This manuscript is currently under review
summary: Low-dimensional representations produced by dimensionality reduction (DR) are commonly evaluated using distortion measures such as trustworthiness and continuity. In this paper, we study the sensitivity of DR methods to plausible input variations by quantifying changes in structural preservation and visually diagnosing how these changes manifest in the resulting representations. This perspective reflects the fact that real-world datasets are finite, noisy samples of an underlying distribution, and DR should not produce substantially different structures under small data changes. We introduce a model-agnostic, perturbation-driven sensitivity evaluation framework that treats perturbations as controlled probes of plausible data variation. Across multiple perturbation families and strength levels, we repeatedly perturb the input, apply a DR method, and evaluate the resulting low-dimensional representations using a set of distortion measures to derive sensitivity profiles for each DR method. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through case studies on DR method comparison, behavior analysis, and robustness improvement. We find that methods performing well according to conventional distortion measures (e.g., t-SNE) can still exhibit substantial sensitivity, leading to instability in visually salient structures such as trajectories and clusters, while certain methods (e.g., multidimensional scaling) may exhibit improved structural preservation under specific perturbations. These results highlight the importance of sensitivity analysis for comparing DR methods, diagnosing perturbation-sensitive visual patterns, and guiding the development of more robust DR methods toward trustworthy visual analytics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一个模型无关、扰动驱动的敏感性评估框架：对输入施加多类不同强度的扰动后反复运行降维方法，并用 trustworthiness、continuity 等失真度量量化结构保持程度的变化，形成各方法的敏感性画像，用于方法比较、不稳定视觉结构诊断与鲁棒性改进。

title: Casper: A Projection-Based Neurosymbolic Layer for Scalable & Guaranteed Constraint Satisfaction
summary: Many real-world problems demand exact constraint satisfaction to be meaningfully solved, yet existing neurosymbolic methods face a stark trade-off: those that guarantee satisfaction fail to scale, while those that scale must resort to approximation. Meanwhile, traditional deep learning approaches offer no satisfaction guarantees at all. In this paper, we propose Casper, a neurosymbolic layer that simultaneously (i) guarantees constraint satisfaction, (ii) scales at inference time, (iii) is fully automated, requiring no problem-specific engineering, and (iv) is fully differentiable, making it composable with any neural predictor both at training and at inference time. Casper casts constraint satisfaction as a closed-form Euclidean projection onto the constraint-feasible region, computable in a single forward pass. Experiments across MNIST arithmetic (up to 1024 digits), Sudoku solving, and Warcraft pathfinding show that Casper is the only method that produces guaranteed-valid outputs at scale: on $30\times30$ Warcraft grids, exact baselines time out and approximate ones produce valid paths less than 7% of the time, while Casper produces them 100% of the time.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Casper 神经符号层：把约束满足写成到可行域的闭式欧氏投影，单次前向即可完成，且完全可微，可与任意神经预测器在训练和推理时组合；在 MNIST 算术、数独和 Warcraft 寻路上验证其可扩展且保证约束满足。

title: DiffER$^2$: Diffusion Ensembles for Retrosynthesis Prediction with SMILES Adapted Particle Guidance
summary: Computational retrosynthesis prediction has the potential to reduce development time for newly discovered drugs by automatically generating potential reactions for a target product. Data-driven approaches commonly treat this as a sequence-to-sequence generation task on SMILES strings. In this work, we construct ensembles of discrete-time and continuous-time diffusion models for molecular generation and incorporate guidance mechanisms for improved output diversity. We propose an adaptation of particle guidance to SMILES sequence generation which significantly improves the number of unique molecules generated by diffusion ensembles while increasing top-k accuracy. These results further expand the efficacy of discrete diffusion for SMILES generation, and our empirical analyses offer new insights into the capabilities of diffusion models for chemical retrosynthesis.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把逆合成预测当作 SMILES 序列生成任务，构建离散时间与连续时间扩散模型集成，并将 particle guidance 适配到 SMILES 序列，以在提升唯一分子数的同时提高 top-k 准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其离散序列扩散采样与粒子引导控制多样性的做法，可能为 LVR 中扩散式 latent 推理状态生成及采样多样性—精度权衡提供可供核查的线索，但任务属化学序列生成，与视觉证据无直接联系，需较多核查。

title: ProPolar: Progressive Polar Decomposition for Implicit Neural Representations
summary: Implicit neural representations (INRs) capture global low-frequency structure during the early stage of training and then refine localized high-frequency details, afterwards. However, standard optimizers are agnostic to the coarse-to-fine learning behavior of INRs. Such optimizers accumulate a gradient matrix in momentum buffer and retain components misaligned with the dominant low-frequency directions in the early stage. We propose a progressively growing rank scheduler and a rank-aware learning-rate scheduler for enhancing a subspace-based momentum optimization, where a momentum matrix is updated within a low-rank subspace. The rank schedule expands the subspace during training, and the scheduler holds the peak learning rate through rank growth so that the added subspace contributes to fine-detail recovery. Experiments on image fitting, single-image super-resolution (SISR), and neural radiance field optimization show that the proposed method improves convergence and peak reconstruction quality over competitive optimizers. The largest gains appear in the high-frequency refinement stage, mirroring the coarse-to-fine progression that the rank schedule targets. A significant study on hyperparameter optimization (HPO) on NeRF further confirms that these gains persist under matched search budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ProPolar，在低秩子空间内更新动量矩阵的优化器基础上加入渐进增长秩调度与秩感知学习率调度，以匹配隐式神经表示由粗到细的学习过程，并在图像拟合、单图超分与 NeRF 优化上验证收敛与重建质量提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其「低秩子空间动量＋随训练渐进扩大秩」的思路可能可供核查：latent 推理状态是否也能表示为随推理进度扩张的低秩工作区并据此设计更新与调度。

title: Trigger-Invariant Contrastive Unlearning for Backdoor Removal
comment: An extended version of the short paper published at CIKM 2026 (https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3799682.3839969)
summary: Backdoor attacks pose a severe threat to modern NLP models by embedding hidden triggers that induce malicious behavior at inference time. Recent unlearning methods such as gradient ascent (GA) attempt to remove backdoors by maximizing the loss on poisoned samples; however, these methods can suffer from a critical limitation: they may shift the trigger's influence to other classes rather than eliminating it. In this work, we propose Trigger-Invariant Contrastive Unlearning (TICU), a framework for mitigating textual backdoor behavior by enforcing prediction and representation invariance to trigger insertion. TICU constructs clean and trigger-inserted counterfactual pairs, then fine-tunes the model so that both inputs produce consistent output distributions and aligned hidden representations. To preserve clean-task performance, TICU also retains the supervised classification loss on clean data and constrains parameter drift from the original model. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets, model architectures, and attack settings show that TICU improves triggered accuracy and reduces trigger-induced prediction shifts compared with existing baselines, while maintaining competitive label-flipping performance and limiting clean-task degradation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TICU：构造干净与含触发词的反事实样本对，通过微调使两者输出分布一致、隐表示对齐，并保留干净数据的监督损失与参数漂移约束，以去除文本后门而不显著损害正常分类性能。

title: SEEL: Towards End-to-End 3D Sign Generation with Language Models
summary: 3D sign language generation aims to produce signing motion from written text. Motivated by the linguistic nature of sign language, recent methods combine a motion tokenizer with a language model to predict motion tokens from text. However, both components are optimized through a two-stage pipeline with mismatched objectives: the tokenizer minimizes reconstruction error in isolation, while the generator learns from rigid one-hot reference tokens. A straightforward end-to-end extension bridges discrete token selection with straight-through estimators (STE), suffering from biased gradients and codebook collapse. To address these limitations, we propose SEEL, an end-to-end framework that aligns tokenization and generation with motion quality through two complementary mechanisms. First, to overcome rigid one-hot supervision, reconstruction-aware generation decodes candidate tokens in context and converts their 3D motion errors into soft targets, guiding the generator with physical motion quality. Second, to propagate generation feedback without STE, generation-aware tokenization passes continuous codebook expectations through the frozen generator, routing generated-motion gradients to the tokenizer to prevent codebook collapse. Combining both mechanisms enables the tokenizer and generator to co-evolve, achieving state-of-the-art performance on CSL-Daily, How2Sign, and Phoenix-2014T. Code and models will be released to facilitate future research.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SEEL，用「重建感知生成」把候选 motion token 的 3D 重建误差转成软目标，并用「生成感知分词」将连续 codebook 期望穿过冻结生成器回传梯度，实现 3D 手势生成的 tokenizer 与语言模型端到端协同训练，避免 STE 偏差与码本坍缩。

title: Amortizing Exact Orthogonality: Drift-Triggered Restoration for Orthogonal Fine-Tuning
summary: Orthogonal finetuning (OFT) adapts a pretrained weight by an orthogonal transform and preserves its singular values and row angles, but existing methods construct an exact or approximate orthogonal transform at every optimization step. We measure how far a transform $A$ is from orthogonal by its orthogonality defect $\|A^\top A-I\|_2$. For OFTv2, which truncates a Cayley-Neumann series, we show that the truncation order does not determine the defect. At its default order, block defects in checkpoints from the reference implementation span five orders of magnitude. We propose Restarted Tangent Orthogonal Finetuning (RTOFT), which uses the first-order update $W(I+S)$ of a weight $W$ with a skew-symmetric $S$ and restores exact orthogonality by a polar decomposition only when the drift $\|S\|_2$ reaches a tolerance $τ$. The defect of $I+S$ is exactly $\|S\|_2^2$. Therefore, reading the drift after every update and restoring before the next forward pass guarantees a defect of at most $τ^2$ in every forward pass, independently of the loss, data, model, and optimizer. A final restoration makes the returned transform exactly orthogonal. On GLUE, RTOFT reduces the training time of block-diagonal, subspace, and butterfly parameterizations from $1.10$-$1.58\times$ to $0.97$-$1.13\times$ that of LoRA, and its block-diagonal version exceeds LoRA by $1.98\pm0.39$ points on the six-task average over five seeds. At $τ=0.10$, the largest drift read during training stays between $0.10$ and $0.12$ across DeBERTaV3, Qwen, and diffusion models, whereas it ranges from $0.17$ to $1.65$ when restoring once per epoch. In all seven settings of our ablation, the tangent update is worse without restoration than with it, and restoring after every step yields no measurable accuracy gain over restoring at the tolerance and costs $4.5$-$27.5\%$ more per step.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析正交微调（OFT）中变换偏离正交性的缺陷，指出 OFTv2 截断阶数并不决定缺陷大小，并提出 RTOFT：用一阶切向更新，仅当漂移「S」超过容差时才用极分解恢复精确正交，从而在每次前向保证缺陷有界，并在 GLUE 上以更低训练开销超过 LoRA。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「持续读取漂移、仅在达容差时投影回约束流形」的更新—校正机制，可能为循环/多步 latent 推理中受限状态或权重几何量的漂移控制提供可供核查的线索，但原文面向纯文本与扩散模型的参数高效微调，未涉及视觉或多模态推理。

title: Pretraining for Forecasting in Relational Databases
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Temporal Systems: From Forecasting to World Modeling
summary: Real-world forecasting increasingly relies on asynchronous transaction logs in relational databases rather than uniformly sampled arrays. While relational deep learning (RDL) models can forecast from these complex histories, they are typically trained separately for each specific target and root entity type. We introduce Query-Conditioned Relational pretraining (QCRP), a self-supervised framework that enables a standard RDL backbone to act as a universal forecaster across a database. QCRP generates diverse forecasting objectives using a structured temporal query grammar and interleaves them through a shared conditional predictor. This produces a robust, frozen encoder reusable for downstream tasks via lightweight predictors or a zero-shot interface. Evaluated on large-scale RelBench databases, QCRP learns frozen representations that support competitive forecasting across tasks and entity types. Furthermore, a single unified QCRP model checkpoint is competitive with isolated, entity-specific specialists. We demonstrate promising results for reusing the learned representations from standard RDL backbones for forecasting tasks in relational databases.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 QCRP，用结构化时间查询语法自动生成多样化预测目标，并通过共享的条件预测器交错进行自监督预训练，使标准 RDL 骨干的冻结编码器可跨任务与实体类型预测，在 RelBench 上与专用模型相当。
AI.relevance_reason: 「查询条件化 + 多目标共享预测器 + 冻结编码器复用」可能为 LVR 中按任务查询条件化并复用 latent 状态、以及监督目标的组合方式提供可核查线索，但研究对象是关系数据库时序预测，不含视觉或多模态推理，迁移价值需人工判断。

title: Linear-Time Online Visual Geometry Transformer with Hybrid Architecture
summary: Transformer-based 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT and $π^3$ predict cameras, depth and point maps directly from many input views. Causal attention models such as StreamVGGT extend them to online video but cache all past tokens, so their total compute grows quadratically with the stream length. Recurrent models such as CUT3R and TTT3R keep a fixed-size state at constant cost, but they progressively forget early geometry. We present LinearVGGT, a hybrid model distilled from StreamVGGT, which uses Mamba2 layers for efficient sequence modeling in three of every four global layers. The remaining layers use register-guided sparse attention to retrieve a few relevant past frames, compensating for the limited exact long-range recall of Mamba2. Our distillation needs only 9\% of the GPU hours and 31\% of the training frames that StreamVGGT uses to learn from VGGT. LinearVGGT keeps an almost constant latency of 27 ms per frame over 1,024 frames and is on average $12 \times$ faster than StreamVGGT. It outperforms its teacher and is competitive with the state-of-the-art streaming model LingBot-Map, while running $2.5\times$ faster and using $2.7\times$ less memory.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LinearVGGT：从 StreamVGGT 蒸馏的混合架构在线视觉几何 Transformer，四分之三全局层改用 Mamba2 做序列建模，其余层用 register 引导的稀疏注意力回取少量相关历史帧，从而在多视图流上以近恒定成本输出相机、深度与点图。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定大小循环状态＋稀疏回取过去帧」的组合及对早期几何被逐步遗忘的分析，可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节在内部状态的保留、证据筛选与长序列下计算—记忆权衡。

title: Fine-Grained Ego-Vehicle Action Recognition from Driving Video
summary: Fine-grained ego-vehicle action recognition turns large-scale driving video into structured, searchable driving scenarios, providing a foundation for discovering critical maneuvers and systematically developing and evaluating autonomous driving models. However, large-scale driving videos often lack explicit ego-action labels, and existing datasets vary in action definitions, annotation granularity, and available supervision. We introduce EgoManeuver, a unified benchmark of 16 lateral and 6 longitudinal actions constructed from seven public driving datasets. Our multi-source labeling system leverages existing annotations and complementary evidence available in each source dataset, including vehicle signals, ego poses, HD-map topology, and captions, to assign labels under a unified fine-grained action taxonomy. We further standardize temporal action boundaries across datasets and validate the resulting labels through kinematic consistency checks and targeted human review. The resulting benchmark contains 86.6K segments spanning 190.8 h across 26 countries and provides a long-tail-aware evaluation protocol. We also introduce DenseEgo, a video-based baseline that combines spatially aware representations with dense per-step action supervision. On the EgoManeuver, DenseEgo achieves 82.7 lateral and 83.5 longitudinal mAP, outperforming the strongest existing video model by 1.5 and 5.0 points, respectively. Finally, we demonstrate one way to integrate DenseEgo with a language-model agent for retrieving driving videos that match user-specified actions and scenarios. All code, datasets, and model weights will be publicly released.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 EgoManeuver 统一基准，将七个公开驾驶数据集按统一细粒度分类体系（16 类横向、6 类纵向动作）重新标注并校准时序边界，另提出结合空间感知表示与稠密逐步监督的视频基线 DenseEgo 及长尾评估协议。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稠密逐步动作监督」加时序边界标准化的做法，可能与 LVR 中逐步 latent 监督的标注粒度与信用分配问题相关，可供核查；但任务本身是驾驶动作识别基准，不涉及视觉推理或 latent 状态生成。

title: Recall4D: Forgetting, Not Misalignment, Limits Long-Horizon Feed-Forward 4D Reconstruction
comment: 20 pages, 10 figures, 15 tables. Project page: https://kincin.github.io/Recall4D/
summary: Feed-forward 4D trackers recover camera motion, depth, and point trajectories from short video clips, but chaining windows over long videos degrades their accuracy. We find that replacing inter-window alignment with ground-truth transforms leaves tracking error essentially unchanged. Static-point error instead grows with time since last observation: repeatedly predicting a static point from windows that no longer observe it corrupts previously recovered geometry. We call this failure forgetting. Merely retaining the last observed positions of unseen points reduces error by 26% on PointOdyssey without modifying the tracker. We introduce Recall4D, a training-free framework that augments a frozen tracker with a persistent world state and sparse motion anchors. Static points retain their world-space positions outside the camera view and are refined by averaging observations decoded at sparse keyframes while in view. For dynamic objects, the tracker decodes sparse representative anchors, while geometric skinning propagates their displacements to dense queries. Across two long-horizon benchmarks, Recall4D improves the accuracy of its backbone while running 7.6-9.0$\times$ faster, and its accuracy gains carry over to five further backbones and three other long-sequence tasks, demonstrating its generality.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文诊断长视频前馈 4D 重建的分窗串联误差，将其归因于未观测静态点的信息「遗忘」，并提出免训练的持久世界状态与稀疏运动锚点来保留和更新几何。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「持久世界状态＋稀疏锚点＋反复观测修正」可能为 LVR 中长期保留视觉证据、抑制隐性状态遗忘与信息坍缩提供可核查的状态维护线索，但需判断能否迁移到多模态推理。

title: Look at What Matters: Learning Lesion Prototypes from Severity Labels for Domain-Generalized Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
summary: Deep learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading often generalize poorly to unseen imaging domains, in part because predictions may exploit correlations specific to source datasets rather than retinal pathology. We address this challenge by constructing grading decisions from lesion evidence learned using only image severity labels. Clinical implications of DR grades provide multiple instance constraints that guide competitive learning of lesion and background prototypes at multiple scales. An additive ordinal scoring model then predicts severity exclusively from individual lesion prototype responses, explicitly connecting learned evidence with grading decisions without a global feature classification pathway. To improve the reliability of this evidence, we introduce teacher guided preservation under image degradations and spatial regularization against persistent coordinate preferences. Across six public DR datasets under a leave one domain out protocol, our method attains a mean quadratic weighted kappa of 0.761, outperforming the strongest competing method by 0.036. Localization and prototype removal analyses show that the learned responses align with retinal lesions and contribute to grading decisions. Experiments across five other prototype architectures and under image degradations further demonstrate the generality and robustness of the approach.

AI.brief_summary: 该文面向糖尿病视网膜病变分级，仅用图像严重度标签学习多尺度病灶与背景原型，并通过加性序数评分模型直接由病灶原型响应给出等级预测，辅以退化下的教师引导保持与空间正则，在六个公开数据集上验证跨域泛化与原型定位。
AI.relevance_reason: 其取消全局特征分类路径、强制答案由原型证据加性汇总的做法，及原型移除分析，可能为核查 VLM 推理是否真正使用视觉 latent 证据、如何分配证据贡献提供参照，但任务领域与多模态推理相距较远，需核查迁移可行性。

title: Faster and Better Query (FBQ): Learning Future-Position Probes from the First Generated Token
summary: When a large language model (LLM) evicts prompt keys and values at the end of prefill, it must decide what to keep before it sees the queries from subsequent decoding steps. Generating a draft continuation can approximate those queries at the cost of extra autoregressive steps. Can we use the embedding of the first output token, already available from the final prefill logits, to construct low-cost pseudo queries that approximate future decoding queries? We start with FTQ-8, which places eight copies of the first token ID at consecutive future positions and reads their attention to the prompt in one causal forward pass. Each copy sees a different prefix, but a generic opening such as the offers a poor literal guess for seven successive tokens. Faster and Better Query (FBQ) preserves the first embedding and learns an additive offset at each of the seven remaining positions. We train these offsets to predict the average prompt attention of a full-cache continuation. On LongBench, FBQ performs comparably to eight-step Lookahead Q-Cache at the same cache budget, using a single forward pass to compute all probe queries.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 LLM 预填阶段结束时淘汰 KV cache 的取舍问题，提出 FBQ：保留首 token 的 embedding，为后续七个位置各学一个加性偏移，构造低成本的伪 query，用一次前向近似完整缓存续写时的 prompt 注意力分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 以单个已生成 token 的表示加可学习偏移来外推未来若干步的注意力/证据需求，可能为 LVR 中「用有限状态预测后续 LOOK 证据需求、按预算筛选视觉证据」提供可核查的方法线索，但对象是纯文本 KV cache，与视觉推理的联系需自行判断。

title: GeoTex: Geometry-as-Texture Encoding and History-Grounded 4D Occupancy Forecasting
summary: 4D occupancy forecasting models 3D scene evolution to support future prediction and scenario generation in autonomous-driving world models. Semantic occupancy abstracts image color and texture into discrete labels, leaving 3D voxel arrangements as the primary cues for distinguishing local shapes within each class. Existing methods borrow image-encoding frameworks to obtain compact latent representations through height channelization or plane factorization, but do not sufficiently model within-column height patterns and cross-column relations jointly before compression, weakening these geometric cues. Forecasting also underutilizes complementary history and struggles to retain reliable observation evidence. We therefore propose GeoTex, an occupancy world model combining geometry-as-texture encoding with history-grounded forecasting. GeoTex Representation jointly encodes within-column height patterns and cross-column relations into compact continuous latent representations and restores 3D structure through content-dependent height unfolding and geometric interaction. GeoTex Prediction retains initial evidence throughout rollout in fixed cross-observation relational memory and incorporates complementary recent history through target-referenced residual updates. After prediction training, decoder-only adaptation improves semantic decoding of predicted states. GeoTex improves average forecasting mIoU and IoU by 9.79% and 11.91% relative to GenieDrive while reducing parameters from 3.47M to 2.33M, with gains increasing at longer horizons. Code is included in the supplementary material.

AI.brief_summary: GeoTex 是面向自动驾驶的 4D 占据预测世界模型，把列内高度模式与跨列关系在压缩前联合编码为紧凑 latent，并用固定跨观测关系记忆保留初始观测证据、通过残差更新引入近期历史，最后用 decoder-only 适配改进预测状态的语义解码。
AI.relevance_reason: 「压缩前联合建模几何线索」与「rollout 中固定记忆持续保留初始证据」可能为 LVR 关注的视觉信息坍缩、证据保留与长程状态更新提供可核查的方法线索，但其任务是占据预测而非视觉推理，迁移性需人工判断。

title: P-FedSkill: A Personalized Federated Skill Learning Framework under Task Heterogeneity
summary: Skill learning has become an important way to improve agent performance. However, agent trajectories often contain sensitive information and cannot be shared across clients, hindering collaborative skill learning. To tackle this issue, federated skill learning (FSL) has emerged as a solution by distilling trajectories into compact skill representations and uploading them to a central server for sharing. However, existing FSL methods typically share skills based on skill similarity without considering their contributions to heterogeneous tasks across clients, thereby degrading agent performance. To address this challenge, we propose P-FedSkill, a personalized FSL framework that comprises three key components: local skill extraction (LSE), personalized skill selection (PSS), and task-aware skill routing (TASR). Specifically, LSE first extracts skill patches (i.e., task applicability conditions and execution strategies) and task execution outcomes from trajectories. PSS then uses these outcomes to evaluate each skill patch's performance on client tasks and incorporates its task applicability condition to construct a personalized skill set for each client. Finally, TASR adaptively selects a task-relevant subset of skill patches based on their applicability conditions to guide agent execution. We further provide a theoretical guarantee for personalized skill selection in P-FedSkill, and extensive experiments also demonstrate its effectiveness.

AI.brief_summary: 提出个性化联邦技能学习框架 P-FedSkill，从智能体轨迹中抽取「技能片段」（任务适用条件与执行策略），按各客户端任务表现筛选个性化技能集，并在执行时依据适用条件路由相关片段，附理论保证与实验。

title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
summary: World models predict what happens under an action, but choosing between actions requires comparing their outcomes in the same physical situation. Factual transitions alone determine action-wise marginal futures and average effects, but not individual effects or the probability that switching actions causes harm. We introduce WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for manipulation that couples candidate futures through shared latent physics and transition noise inferred from factual history. Each candidate action induces a sparse object-factor causal graph describing the physical pathways it activates. Rolling out these graphs under the shared situation anchors predictions to observed outcomes and confines action contrasts to the objects each action reaches. Shared type-conditioned functions support varying numbers of objects, while a round-trip loss enforces action-invariant abduction without counterfactual labels. We show that replacing an individual effect with its conditional mean incurs mean-squared error equal to its conditional variance, motivating comparisons between coupled futures. Building on these comparisons, Counterfactual Advantage Planning (CAP) ranks plans by their advantage over an incumbent within shared situations and constrains the probability of harm. Paired advantages reduce estimator variance by a factor of $1-ρ$, where $ρ$ is the correlation between branch outcomes, and cancel model errors shared by both branches. Each executed transition provides hindsight advantages to update the physics posterior, the next plan, and an amortized policy without a learned critic. We further establish when observational transitions identify interventional dynamics. Paired simulator interventions evaluate counterfactual accuracy, graph recovery, compositional generalization, and decision quality.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 WhatIf 反事实世界模型：用共享 latent physics 和从事实历史推断的转移噪声耦合多个候选未来，每个动作诱导稀疏的物体因子因果图，并以 round-trip 损失在无反事实标签下训练动作不变的 abduction，再据此做反事实优势规划。

title: REFORGE: LLM-Assisted RTL Bug Repair with Structured Context and Verification Feedback
comment: Accepted at DATE 2027 (Design, Automation and Test in Europe); initial author version
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can write and repair RTL, but successful compilation or testbench execution does not establish defect removal, behavioral preservation, security, or implementation feasibility. Existing LLM-based RTL repair methods often report a single repair rate without retaining separate evidence for these properties, limiting reproducible comparison and integration into hardware design flows. We present REFORGE, which, to our knowledge, is the first LLM-assisted RTL repair framework that maintains and accumulates structured repair evidence across iterations, allowing it to generate fixes that satisfy multiple objectives simultaneously, including functionality, behavioral equivalence, security, and cost efficiency. REFORGE profiles buggy RTL, identifies structural and security-relevant features, localizes failing behavior, and uses verification-guided diagnosis to generate complete RTL repair variants. Each variant undergoes syntax checking, simulation, formal analysis, off-trigger preservation, security re-scan, and synthesis-based power, performance, and area analysis. We implement REFORGE as a backend-independent repair-and-verification flow and evaluate it in 288 runs across three LLM backends and three benchmark suites. On CirFix, the proposed context and diagnosis increase runs delivering a checked repair from 32/63 to 51/63, while every configuration repairs the Hack@DAC OpenTitan defect. Evidence records also show that a testbench-only criterion reports 3.9 times more repairs than the full set of applicable checks, security-clean outputs may lack functional verification, and different RTL repairs can implement equivalent hardware. These results show that LLM-generated RTL repairs require explicit multi-stage verification evidence rather than a single pass/fail outcome.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 REFORGE，一个 LLM 辅助的 RTL 缺陷修复框架：跨迭代累积结构化修复证据，经语法检查、仿真、形式验证、安全重扫与综合 PPA 多阶段验证后再产出修复变体，并在三种 LLM 后端与三个基准上做评估。
